rv.q: In a pitch-perfect production from Sam Mendes, it is devastatingly moving, bitterly funny, tender, cruel and wise.
It’s now nine-tenths of a superb one.
If it’s not faultless writing, I’d still say ‘The Hills of California’ handily clears that bar.
The West End is infinitely the richer for its presence.
Jez Butterworth’s eagerly awaited new drama...close to sweeping us off our feet
Butterworth has done it again with his new play The Hills of California.
The dialogue is zippy, the humor sharp, dark and irreverent.
Absolutely remarkable and a must-see for anyone who loves theatre or just loves humanity.
Together, the duo have once again brought us a gorgeously textured performance that drifts across time and tone.

cn.t: Butterworth and Mendes deliver a richly textured, emotionally resonant family drama that unfolds with novelistic depth. Critics praise its warmth, raw truths about grief, and hypnotic performances in this enthralling Blackpool-set saga.
